## feature

<!-- new capability this task added -->

### v0.3.0 published on GitHub

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The tag is pushed, the release page exists with the curated body, and the version bump is verified in three places and by the CLI.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Version `0.2.0 → 0.3.0` in `pyproject.toml`, `pixi.toml`, `src/sam_tagger/__init__.py`.
2. Commit `chore(release): bump version to 0.3.0` (`aa52fcc`), annotated tag `v0.3.0` on it, `main` and tag pushed.
3. GitHub Release `v0.3.0` created with curated notes that document the `to_*` columns and the N-base caveat.

#### before

The GitHub remote sat at `v0.2.0` and `main` was 2 commits behind the local repository, so the `to_*` columns existed only locally.

#### after

The remote `main` carries the feature and the bump, and the release page publishes the schema change for downstream users.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

```text
0.3.0
[main aa52fcc] chore(release): bump version to 0.3.0
To https://github.com/jiangyun-fun/sam-tagger.git
   f2b02f3..aa52fcc  main -> main
 * [new tag]         v0.3.0 -> v0.3.0
https://github.com/jiangyun-fun/sam-tagger/releases/tag/v0.3.0
```

- `pixi run -e dev sam-tagger --version` → `0.3.0`.

:::

## caveat

### semver choice assumes the repo follows 0.x minor bumps for features

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

v0.2.0 used a minor bump for a feature-plus-breaking change, which supports but does not prove the convention for a pure additive feature.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. I chose `0.3.0` because new output columns are a user-visible feature, not a repair.
2. A maintainer preferring `0.2.1` would need to re-cut the tag.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `git log -1 --format='%s' v0.2.0` → `chore(release): bump version to 0.2.0`.

:::

## assumption

### release notes body is acceptable as written

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The body follows the v0.2.0 release style and states the semantics verified by tests, but the user has not reviewed it yet.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The notes name the four columns, the `to_x` semantics, and the N-base caveat.
2. The user can edit the body on the release page without re-tagging.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `gh release view v0.3.0 --json body` returns the curated text (section headers `## error.parquet: mismatch split by read base`).

:::

## conclusion

### the released artifact carries the to_* columns

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The tag points at the bump commit that follows the feature commit, and the CLI reports the new version from the tagged source tree.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `v0.3.0` = `aa52fcc`, whose parent chain contains `9819fe4` (feature) and `1df9436` (docs).
2. Downstream conda recipes can consume the sdist and wheel once the workflow attaches them.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `git describe --exact-match HEAD` → `v0.3.0`.

:::

## recommendation

### L: notify error.parquet consumers of the wider schema

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The schema change is additive but visible, and any strict-schema consumer breaks on the new columns. I have not audited who those consumers are.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Point downstream users of `error.parquet` at the v0.3.0 release notes before they upgrade.
